value.text:
The Institute of Scientific Research and Revival of Islamic Heritage (معهد البحوث العلمية وإحياء التراث الإسلامي) is a government research institute affiliated with Umm Al-Qura University in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. Its work includes collecting, cataloguing, editing, studying and publishing Islamic heritage materials, alongside research undertaken through centres in several fields.

Its institutional origins are associated with the Center for Scientific Research and Revival of Islamic Heritage, established in 1396 AH. The institute itself was established in 1406 AH and incorporated the earlier centre. The chronology therefore distinguishes the foundation of the centre from the later creation of the institute. These dates are expressed in the Hijri calendar.

The institute's research centres cover Islamic studies and education, Arabic language and literature, educational and psychological sciences, social sciences, applied sciences, engineering and architecture, medicine, and pharmaceutical sciences. Its research services include supporting and funding scientific projects, publishing books, research and university theses, and making manuscript reproductions available to researchers. A research design and statistical consultation unit assists researchers with study design and statistical analysis. These activities place manuscript preservation and scholarly publishing alongside support for research across the university's disciplines.
